function: Adaptive downlink CSI sensing in FDD: designs next pilot precoder from past PMI/CQI feedback, recovers the CSI, and quantizes CQI with a learnable quantizer (pp. 2-4).
system: FDD downlink; BS with Nt=32 antennas, single-antenna UE; Type-I codebook Nv=512, Na=32; no RIS; frequency band not stated, other settings deferred to [12, Table I] (p. 4).
method: TransenseCSI: Transformer-inspired multi-head attention network with sequential precoder and CSI recovery modules plus learnable linear quantizer; supervised learning (NMSEr loss), quantized variant fine-tuned (pp. 3-5).
data_channel: DeepMIMO CSI dataset with Nt=32, configuration as in [12, Table I]; 600 training, 400 validation, 1000 test samples; noise augmentation at 20 dB SNR (pp. 4-5).
test_conditions: Same DeepMIMO dataset for training and testing (600/400/1000 split); a separate model trained for each number of rounds T=1..10; no new scenario or configuration (p. 5).
baselines: Non-learned: PRIME, AM-based PR, CPR, Type-I and Type-II codebooks; learned: LSTM scheme modified from [9]; quantizers: Uniform-Q and learned PQB [16] (pp. 5-6).
metrics: NMSEr (normalized MSE with common phase rotation, in dB) versus the number of sensing rounds T, for ideal and quantized CQI feedback (pp. 4-6).
complexity: none; only qualitative claims of a lightweight network and a computationally efficient quantizer (pp. 3, 6).
openness: Code at https://github.com/chitar/TransenseCSI (footnote 3, p. 5); public DeepMIMO dataset (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "The performance is evaluated over the DeepMIMO CSI dataset" (DeepMIMO ray-tracing channels, Nt = 32), used for training and testing.
q2_support: p. 5: "The number of samples for training, validation and testing are 600, 400 and 1000, respectively"; one dataset, no new scenario, band or antenna setting, and "TransenseCSI is initially trained by using the Adam optimizer for 3000 epochs" for each T.
q3_support: p. 5: "we also implement an LSTM-based scheme which is modified from the one in [9]" besides PRIME, AM-based PR, CPR and Type-II; "TransenseCSI surpasses LSTM, achieving a 2 dB lower NMSEr at T = 4".
q4_support: p. 3: "TransenseCSI always keeps a lightweight NN regardless of the increase of T" and p. 6: "not only computationally efficient"; both qualitative, no FLOPs, parameter count, runtime or complexity order is reported.
q5_support: p. 5: "The codes are available at https://github.com/chitar/TransenseCSI"; p. 4, footnote: https://www.deepmimo.net/ for the public DeepMIMO dataset.
notes: Included, area 2: CSI sensing (adaptive pilot precoder plus CSI recovery from PMI/CQI feedback), main metric NMSEr. The PDF is the paper of the DOI (title and DOI on p. 1). Table I (p. 4) and Figs. 3 and 4 (pp. 5-6) were read as page images: NMSEr values only, no cost figures. The quantized variant is fine-tuned for 1000 epochs on the same data (p. 5), which is not a test in new conditions.
